requirements.quote: The sending part of a stream that the endpoint initiates (types 0 and 2 for clients, 1 and 3 for servers) is opened by the application.
requirements.condition: An endpoint initiates a stream of type 0 or 2 as a client, or type 1 or 3 as a server.
requirements.required_behavior: The application opens the sending part of the stream.
requirements.why_checkable: The initiator role, stream type, and event that opens the sending part can be observed in stream-creation logic or runtime state transitions.

requirements.quote: The "Ready" state represents a newly created stream that is able to accept data from the application.
requirements.condition: A sending part is newly created and is in the "Ready" state.
requirements.required_behavior: It accepts stream data from the application.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can create a stream, confirm its Ready state, and submit application data before any stream frame is sent.

requirements.quote: Stream data might be buffered in this state in preparation for sending.
requirements.condition: A sending part is in the "Ready" state and receives application data.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation is permitted to buffer the data before sending it.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation can be checked to ensure that buffering application data while the stream remains Ready is accepted behavior.

requirements.quote: Sending the first STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame causes a sending part of a stream to enter the "Send" state.
requirements.condition: The first STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame is sent for a sending part.
requirements.required_behavior: The sending part enters the "Send" state.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame emission and the resulting internal stream state are directly observable in a focused state-transition test.

requirements.quote: An implementation might choose to defer allocating a stream ID to a stream until it sends the first STREAM frame and enters this state
requirements.condition: A locally created stream has not yet sent its first STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation is permitted to defer allocating a stream ID until the first STREAM frame is sent and the stream enters the "Send" state.
requirements.why_checkable: Allocation timing can be inspected or tested relative to first STREAM-frame transmission and entry into Send.

requirements.quote: The sending part of a bidirectional stream initiated by a peer (type 0 for a server, type 1 for a client) starts in the "Ready" state when the receiving part is created.
requirements.condition: A server creates the receiving part of a peer-initiated type 0 bidirectional stream, or a client creates the receiving part of a peer-initiated type 1 bidirectional stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The sending part starts in the "Ready" state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can create the receiving side of the identified peer-initiated stream type and inspect the initial sending-side state.

requirements.quote: In the "Send" state, an endpoint transmits -- and retransmits as necessary -- stream data in STREAM frames.
requirements.condition: A sending part is in the "Send" state and has stream data to transmit or previously transmitted data requiring retransmission.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint transmits or retransmits the stream data in STREAM frames as necessary.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces can verify that stream data and required retransmissions are carried in STREAM frames while the part is in Send.

requirements.quote: The endpoint respects the flow control limits set by its peer
requirements.condition: An endpoint transmits stream data while the sending part is in the "Send" state.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint keeps transmission within the stream flow-control limits set by its peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not transmit stream data beyond the peer-set flow-control limits.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can advertise a known limit and packet output can be checked for offsets or lengths exceeding that limit.

requirements.quote: continues to accept and process MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.
requirements.condition: A sending part is in the "Send" state and a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for it is received.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint accepts and processes the MAX_STREAM_DATA frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not disregard all MAX_STREAM_DATA frames merely because the stream is already in the "Send" state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a larger MAX_STREAM_DATA value in Send and verify that the effective stream send limit is updated.

requirements.quote: An endpoint in the "Send" state generates STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames if it is blocked from sending by stream flow control limits
requirements.condition: An endpoint is in the "Send" state and stream flow-control limits block it from sending.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint generates STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust the stream-level send credit and observe whether a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame is generated.

requirements.quote: After the application indicates that all stream data has been sent and a STREAM frame containing the FIN bit is sent, the sending part of the stream enters the "Data Sent" state.
requirements.condition: The application has indicated that all stream data has been sent and the endpoint sends a STREAM frame containing the FIN bit.
requirements.required_behavior: The sending part enters the "Data Sent" state.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can issue the application completion signal, observe the FIN-bearing STREAM frame, and inspect the resulting state.

requirements.quote: From this state, the endpoint only retransmits stream data as necessary.
requirements.condition: The sending part is in the "Data Sent" state.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint retransmits previously sent stream data when necessary.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not perform new stream-data transmission beyond necessary retransmission.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet output after entry into Data Sent can be compared with previously sent ranges to distinguish retransmission from new data.

requirements.quote: The endpoint does not need to check flow control limits or send STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames for a stream in this state.
requirements.condition: A stream's sending part is in the "Data Sent" state.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation is permitted to omit flow-control-limit checks and STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED generation for that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation can verify that an implementation remains conformant when those checks and frame generations are omitted in Data Sent.

requirements.quote: The endpoint can safely ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA frames it receives from its peer for a stream in this state.
requirements.condition: The endpoint receives a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame from its peer for a stream whose sending part is in the "Data Sent" state.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to ignore the MAX_STREAM_DATA frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject MAX_STREAM_DATA in Data Sent and verify that ignoring it does not alter the stream's required behavior or state.

requirements.quote: Once all stream data has been successfully acknowledged, the sending part of the stream enters the "Data Recvd" state
requirements.condition: All stream data has been successfully acknowledged.
requirements.required_behavior: The sending part enters the "Data Recvd" state.
requirements.why_checkable: Acknowledgment processing can be driven until every sent data range is acknowledged, after which the state can be inspected.

requirements.quote: the "Data Recvd" state, which is a terminal state.
requirements.condition: The sending part has entered the "Data Recvd" state.
requirements.required_behavior: The sending part remains terminal and performs no further state transition.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sending part must not transition out of "Data Recvd".
requirements.why_checkable: State-transition tests can attempt subsequent relevant events and verify that no outgoing transition occurs.

requirements.quote: From any state that is one of "Ready", "Send", or "Data Sent", an application can signal that it wishes to abandon transmission of stream data.
requirements.condition: A sending part is in "Ready", "Send", or "Data Sent".
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation permits the application to signal abandonment of stream-data transmission.
requirements.why_checkable: The application abandonment operation can be invoked independently in each of the three named states.

requirements.quote: In either case, the endpoint sends a RESET_STREAM frame, which causes the stream to enter the "Reset Sent" state.
requirements.condition: While the sending part is in "Ready", "Send", or "Data Sent", either the application signals abandonment or the endpoint receives a STOP_SENDING frame from its peer.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint sends a RESET_STREAM frame and the stream enters the "Reset Sent" state.
requirements.error_behavior: Abandonment or receipt of STOP_SENDING is handled by sending RESET_STREAM and transitioning to "Reset Sent".
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can trigger each antecedent in each applicable state, observe the RESET_STREAM frame, and inspect the resulting state.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MAY send a RESET_STREAM as the first frame that mentions a stream
requirements.condition: No frame sent by the endpoint has yet mentioned the stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to send RESET_STREAM as the first frame mentioning the stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet ordering can be inspected to confirm that a first-mention RESET_STREAM is accepted as valid behavior.

requirements.quote: this causes the sending part of that stream to open and then immediately transition to the "Reset Sent" state.
requirements.condition: The endpoint sends RESET_STREAM as the first frame that mentions a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The sending part opens and then immediately transitions to the "Reset Sent" state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send first-mention RESET_STREAM and inspect both stream creation and its immediate resulting state.

requirements.quote: Once a packet containing a RESET_STREAM has been acknowledged, the sending part of the stream enters the "Reset Recvd" state
requirements.condition: A packet containing the stream's RESET_STREAM frame has been acknowledged.
requirements.required_behavior: The sending part enters the "Reset Recvd" state.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can acknowledge the packet carrying RESET_STREAM and inspect the resulting sending-part state.

requirements.quote: the "Reset Recvd" state, which is a terminal state.
requirements.condition: The sending part has entered the "Reset Recvd" state.
requirements.required_behavior: The sending part remains terminal and performs no further state transition.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sending part must not transition out of "Reset Recvd".
requirements.why_checkable: State-transition tests can deliver subsequent relevant events and verify that the state has no outgoing transition.
